answer: Bonded staking deters Sybil attacks by requiring agents to lock collateral in escrow before participating in market tasks. Gateways terrace these deposit requirements into progressive tiers, acting as an economic jetty that buffers the network against registration floods. An attacker must commit a saffron reserve of scarce tokens per identity, imposing linear capital lockup costs. However, this mechanism favors wealthy incumbents and excludes capital-constrained agents.
